newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai buyers sidelined by high soy, corn prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai buyers sidelined by high soy, corn prices.

text.p: The grain and oilseed market was featureless this week as buyers were sidelined by high Chicago prices, trade sources said.
But they said the upcoming fresh end-rainy season soybean supplies were expected to ease pressure to buy temporarily.
Trade sources projected that 160,000-200,000 tonnes of soybeans would start entering the market from the end of this month.

"The price is not at all attractive. But with some more soymeal coming from India and South America plus local supplies to be available from later this month, we can afford not to buy for some time," said an official of a major feedmill.
Vessel Lissom is expected to arrive here with 20,000 tonnes from Brazil and Argentina by mid-March.
Soymeal from India was being quoted around $320 per tonne c&f Bangkok and US soymeal was indicated at $335 and higher. Local soymeal was steady at 9.55-9.60 baht a kg.
Chicago soybeans rose sharply on concerns about a possible port strike in Brazil and on talk about rain-delayed harvesting of the Brazilian soybean crop, pushing up the prices of other soy products.
The Thai agriculture ministry said that 1996/97 (April-March) soybean output was forecast at 352,279 tonnes.
Corn also surged to a five-month high on fund buying.
But the local industry was unhurt by a rise in corn prices as more domestic supplies were available.

"The price of corn eased this week because of rising supplies and lower demand. More supplies are entering the market but the industry slowed down buying as their silos are mostly full after active buying recently," said an official from Betagro.
The corn price eased to around 4.30 baht a kg from 4.50 baht last week.
